listing.name: Top Gear (SNES) (Top Gear for Windows)
listing.summary: Research listing. Upstream route: Windows/Linux package; partial native conversion Limits: Partial native conversion: translated races, emulated menus/routines. Linux experimentally untested on real machines. Upstream platforms: Windows x86-64 ZIP and experimental Linux x86-64 tar.gz. Linux build untested on real machines upstream; native races retain emulated menus/routines. Original data: Own unmodified Top Gear USA SNES ROM, 524,288 bytes after optional 512-byte copier-header removal, SHA-256 ca9889f17f184b3d99a2eaaa82af73e366f03ed00313fdd369e5e023b208e788. Select it in topgear-launcher or supply it beside/topgear executable; original graphics/audio remain read from that ROM. Portcove setup/gameplay not verified.

steps.title: Keep a permitted completed hybrid player
steps.instruction: Use an already permitted working v0.1.3 Windows x64 topgear.exe copy with its complete creating installation. The publisher documents direct native-player use with your own original. Races use translated C while menus/some routines use LakeSnes; no emulation-free/full-conversion claim. No top-level project license was established; LakeSnes MIT does not license all project/game/package material, and missing optional LICENSE alone is not a private-use prohibition.

steps.title: Keep the exact own USA ROM
steps.instruction: Use your own unmodified Top Gear USA SNES ROM: 524,288 bytes after optional 512-byte copier-header removal, upstream SHA256 ca9889f17f184b3d99a2eaaa82af73e366f03ed00313fdd369e5e023b208e788. Preserve the original and exact actual path for graphics/audio and game data. Upstream checks the input; Core does not extract, patch or authenticate it, and other revisions/translations are not inherited.

steps.title: Select the actual game with one literal original path
steps.instruction: Select topgear.exe itself with one absolute existing owned ROM path as its single literal argument, keeping spaces inside that token, and the actual established writable containing installation-root CWD. The direct native game remains in process. Complete optional settings in topgear-launcher.exe separately; that launcher starts a background game and destroys its process handle without waiting, so it is not the selected Play entry. Do not select tg_headless, --original interpreter-only, replay/verification or build helpers for ordinary translated-race Play.

steps.title: Review intent and keep updates player-owned
steps.instruction: Review and consent to the exact native executable, actual working directory and literal arguments; choose Play separately. Core observes the selected process, not an exclusive family or sandbox. Upstream/player owns setup, profiles, repair and actual replacement. Close every real instance before changing files, keep the old creating copy and review a changed executable through relink. Removing registration removes only metadata and preserves all external files. Keep the creating hybrid/runtime settings; no self-replacement authority, exclusive session or engine/gameplay certification is inferred. Linux packaging remains experimental and untested on real machines upstream, separate from this Windows route.

steps.title: Preserve actual profile, progress and recordings
steps.instruction: Keep the whole runtime and ROM, actual SDL profile %APPDATA%/topgear-pc/Top Gear settings.txt, launcher.txt, progress.txt and ghosts.bin, executable-side controls.txt and recordings/session logs/coverage, custom/replay/mod outputs and unknown files. Preserve custom CWD/profile paths separately. Existing automatic progress/ghost/recording writes remain player/upstream owned; do not move or regenerate them merely to register. Keep old state/runtime together; metadata removal preserves all external bytes. Session recordings can fall back to the actual SDL profile when the executable-side recordings directory cannot be created; preserve both actual locations.
